external_entities.name: All Core Devs
external_entities.description: Ethereum core developer community that makes decisions in regular meetings
external_entities.trust_rationale: Core developers have accountability and reputation but governance decisions still require community consensus and multiple independent implementations

external_entities.name: EIP Authors
external_entities.description: Authors proposing individual EIPs for inclusion in hard forks
external_entities.trust_rationale: Authors are authenticated via GitHub but their proposals still require implementation review, security analysis, and testing

external_entities.name: Client Implementation Teams
external_entities.description: Teams developing Ethereum clients (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon, etc.)
external_entities.trust_rationale: Client teams are known entities with implementation responsibility; their work is reviewed by other teams providing cross-validation

external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
external_entities.description: External client requesting Merkle proofs via JSON-RPC
external_entities.trust_rationale: Any client can request proofs; requests should be validated and rate-limited to prevent DoS

external_entities.name: RPC Provider
external_entities.description: Potentially untrusted JSON-RPC endpoint providing proof data
external_entities.trust_rationale: The entire purpose of eth_getProof is to enable trustless verification; RPC providers may return malicious data but cryptographic proofs make this detectable

external_entities.name: Consensus Layer / Light Client
external_entities.description: Trusted source of block headers (beacon chain, light client sync)
external_entities.trust_rationale: The consensus layer is the source of truth for finalized block headers; if consensus layer is compromised, all downstream security is broken

external_entities.name: Calling Contract
external_entities.description: Smart contract or EOA invoking the RIPEMD-160 precompile
external_entities.trust_rationale: Any contract can call precompiles with arbitrary input data; the precompile must handle any input safely

external_entities.name: Untrusted Data Source
external_entities.description: Any contract or EOA providing data to be hashed
external_entities.trust_rationale: Hash functions are designed to accept arbitrary untrusted input; the precompile produces deterministic output regardless of input

external_entities.name: Block Producer / Validator
external_entities.description: Consensus-layer validator that produced the block
external_entities.trust_rationale: Validators have stake at risk and are authenticated by the consensus layer; their blocks are still fully validated by execution layer

external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer
external_entities.description: Peer node that propagated the block over the network
external_entities.trust_rationale: Network peers can propagate any data; all blocks require full validation regardless of source

external_entities.name: Beacon Chain Consensus Layer
external_entities.description: Consensus layer that originates withdrawal requests
external_entities.trust_rationale: Withdrawal data comes from the beacon chain through authenticated Engine API; if beacon chain is compromised, withdrawals cannot be trusted

misclassified_entities.name: System Contracts
misclassified_entities.description: Protocol-level contracts that generate requests during execution
misclassified_entities.reason: System contracts are internal protocol components deployed at known addresses (e.g., deposit contract). They are part of the trusted execution environment, not external actors sending data from outside the system boundary.

coverage_analysis.notes: EXT-CORE-DEVS, EXT-EIP-AUTHORS, EXT-CLIENT-TEAMS are governance entities without explicit data flow edges in the technical subgraphs. EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-PRAGUE, EXT-P2P-PEER, and EXT-BEACON-CHAIN are mentioned in context but their edges are implicit through state transitions. Cancun LOG instructions (spec_a6202182) has no external entities as all operations are internal EVM execution.
